subject: general
question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2013**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted on **10 September 2013** by the Government of India.
 
• NFSA aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's 1.2 billion people.
 
• Under the NFSA, beneficiaries are entitled to 5 kilograms of food grains per person per month at subsidized prices.
 
• The Act covers up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population under the targeted public distribution system (TPDS).
 
• The identification of eligible households is done by the state governments, while the central government allocates food grains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of NFSA**

 
 
• To provide food and nutritional security by ensuring access to adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices.
 
• To ensure that the most vulnerable sections of the society receive food security.
 
 
 
• **Key Components**
 
 
• **Subsidized Food Grains:** Rice at ₹3 per kg, wheat at ₹2 per kg, and coarse grains at ₹1 per kg.
 
• **Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY):** Provides 35 kg of food grains per month to the poorest of the poor households.
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:** Provides meals to school children to improve nutritional levels.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Challenges**
 
 
• Identification of eligible beneficiaries remains a critical challenge.
 
• Leakages and inefficiencies in the public distribution system (PDS) affect the delivery of benefits.
 
 
 
• **State Involvement**
 
 
• State governments are responsible for the identification of households, issuing ration cards, and ensuring delivery of food grains.
 
• States have the flexibility to implement their own additional food security schemes.
 
 

d4:T
